title: Meta FAIR/NYU: 200+ MLLMs show encoder pretraining optional, vision-only parameters required
summary: An author-posted preprint from Meta FAIR and NYU reports that training 200+ multimodal LLMs from scratch on identical data shows separate vision-encoder pretraining is optional, vision-only parameters are not, and placement of the encoder before the LLM is optional. Encoder pretraining was counted against the same lifetime compute budget; main comparisons used Qwen3-1.7B and 4B backbones with 0.4B parameters of vision capacity, plus a scaling ladder from 0.6B to 6.4B, evaluated on 16 Cambrian VQA benchmarks at 448 px and 12 language benchmarks. Pretrained encoders built with contrastive, self-supervised, and two captioning objectives at best tied a from-scratch encoder at matched compute, and pretraining MetaCLIP 6.5x longer raised ImageNet linear-probe accuracy from 80.4% to 84.4% without improving VQA; encoder-free models trailed at every size and needed about 3x the compute to catch up. The authors&\#x27; "in-fusion" variant adds zero-initialized vision-only attention projections and FFNs to the LLM&\#x27;s first eight layers, matching an encoder from 1.7B to 6.4B with about 13% lower time to first token \(45.0 vs 44.4 VQA at 1.7B\), though these remain preprint claims that have not been peer-reviewed.
